newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ dollar ends steady, off session peak.
newsitem.headline: NZ dollar ends steady, off session peak.

text.p: The New Zealand dollar ended steady but off its session peak after a quiet Monday session.

The Kiwi closed at US$0.6941/48 from its 0.6931/38 open after bidding interest from one local bank took it swiftly up to a high for the day of 0.6956 early in the session. The Trade-Weighted Index ended steady at 68.25.
Dealers were a little surprised by the speed with which the currency ran up and it now appeared to have more of a bid tone.
"We can probably expect the 0.6955 level to continue to be resistance but there are probably still stop losses above that level," said one Auckland dealer.
Downside support should remain at around 0.6930-35 -- about where it closed in New York last week -- he said.

A break from the 0.6935-55 range over the next session appeared unlikely, but this week's Federal Reserve Open Market Committee meeting may have some bearing on local direction, he said. -- James Gray (64 9 302 1253)
